notes:
If you updated to 1.3.66 and Docket asked you to activate a Mac that was
already activated, this is the fix, and nothing was wrong with your licence.

1.3.66 tightened how Docket remembers a licence check, so that a check earned by
one build could not be spent by another. The tightening was too broad: it also
threw away the record of which activation this Mac already holds, which every
copy installed before 1.3.66 keeps in a slightly older format.

With that record discarded, Docket had no way to tell that this Mac was already
one of your three. Asking about your licence reported it as not activated, and
running an audit would have taken a second activation for the same machine.

Docket now separates the two questions properly. Whether the stored record is
about your key decides whether the activation it names can be reused; whether
this build earned the stored verdict decides whether that verdict can be
trusted without asking again. Updating re-checks the activation you already
have, which is one request and costs you nothing.

If 1.3.66 did take a second activation on a Mac you already had, that seat can
be returned — write to the address on the contact page and it will be sorted
out the same day.

Nothing in your audits changes in this release.
